name: Panchali
catalog_citation: Sohil, Shakeel Ahmed. 2018. Phonological Study of the Panchali (Poguli/Khah) Language. Language in India 18(2): 389-405. http://www.languageinindia.com/feb2018/
catalog_quote: Stress is not a distinctive feature of Panchali language. However, since Panchali is a syllable timed language, sometimes individual letters and words are stressed for emphasis. The ordinary meaning of the sentence is changed with some special meaning by giving a stress, e.g. Kut poƮh ʧu! / What beautiful is / What a beautiful is! ... kut ʧu poƮh ? / what is beautiful / What is beautiful? ... Ruka:vi meh/ gatshni d ̓em / You stop not go me / Do not stop / let me go ... ruka:vi/ meh gatshni d ̓em / stop not go me / stop / donot let me go
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: The author (a native speaker, field survey mainly in Ramban district) states that stress is not phonemic/contrastive in Khah (Panchali/Poguli); the only stress he describes is emphatic sentence-level stress on particular words. He does not say on which syllable word-level prominence falls. The suprasegmental inventory he sets up contains junctures, four pitch levels and three terminal contours plus vowel length, and he calls the language 'intonational' (pitch functions at sentence level).
new_statements.exceptions: None; only emphatic/contrastive sentence stress examples are given.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement denies lexical distinctiveness of stress and illustrates stress only at sentence level (emphasis); position of default word stress in citation forms is not described. Vowel length is contrastive (seven short/long pairs). Hook 1987 separately notes lower tone on open vowels after /h/ (phonetic).
new_statements.identity_note: Sohil 2018 describes 'Panchali (Poguli/Khah)' as one language covering Pogal-Paristan, Banihal, Ramsu, Khari/Ukhral tehsils of Ramban district (i.e. Glottolog khah1234 as a whole, dialects Poguli pogu1238, Khasha khas1276, Panchali Khah panc1249, Paristani pari1259); the author is a native speaker from Chacknarwah, Banihal tehsil, so his data lean toward the Khah/Banihal side rather than Pogal valley Poguli proper. Sarazi/Siraji of Doda is a different Glottolog language and was excluded.

However, since Panchali is a syllable timed language, sometimes individual letters and words are stressed for emphasis' -- followed only by sentence-level emphatic-stress examples; no statement of where word stress falls. Suprasegmental inventory lists junctures, pitch levels, terminal contours, vowel length; 'Panchali is an intonational language'.
